purpose: Test whether the already-observed butterfly host-portfolio architecture is geographically replicated across realized butterfly zoogeographic realms.

gbif.taxon_resolution: exact accepted species under the existing chocho resolver
gbif.window_rule: spread deterministic page offsets across the full GBIF result index, capped at the first 100000 searchable records

transport_repair.duplicate_key_rule: if completed transport chunks for one frozen parent window contain the same GBIF occurrence key more than once, retain the first fetched row for that key, record the number removed, and rebuild the parent window; no replacement key is sought
transport_repair.reason: technical response paging can duplicate keys across separately transported chunks; occurrence identity rather than page multiplicity is the sampling unit

realm_source.dataset: CMEC Zoogeographic Realms and Regions — newRealms
realm_source.citation: Holt BG et al. 2013. An Update of Wallace's Zoogeographic Regions of the World. Science 339:74-78.
realm_source.provider: Center for Macroecology, Evolution and Climate, University of Copenhagen
realm_source.execution_rule: download the official CMEC archive, record archive SHA256, read newRealms.shp, retain Realm and geometry, dissolve by Realm, transform to EPSG:4326, record exact derived GeoJSON SHA256 used for assignment

species_realm_summary.primary_realm: realm with the largest mapped-occurrence count; exact count ties are TIE
species_realm_summary.primary_realm_share: largest realm count divided by all realm-mapped occurrence records

tie_handling.informative_count: species with >=30 mapped records remain realm-informative even if the top realm count is tied
tie_handling.realm_replication: TIE is not a realm and is excluded from realm cell counts, the four-realm evaluability criterion, by-realm correlations, and leave-one-realm-out analyses

robustness: leave one primary realm out at a time
report family x primary-realm cell counts without treating cells as independent replication

pooled_within_realm.population: realm-informative expanded host-taxonomy-adequate species with non-TIE primary realm
pooled_within_realm.transform: within each primary realm, replace predictor and response by average percentile ranks on [0,1]
pooled_within_realm.estimand: Pearson correlation across species between within-realm percentile ranks; this is a pooled within-realm rank association

responses.expected_direction: positive from the already-observed global exploratory architecture result
negative from the already-observed global exploratory architecture result

inference.null: host-family breadth is unrelated to portfolio architecture within realized primary realms
inference.permutation: permute host-family-count values independently within each primary realm, preserving realm membership and outcome values

reporting: realm-specific Spearman correlations for all n>=10 realms

claim_boundary: This is a post-hoc generality audit of an already-observed portfolio pattern, not a prospective hypothesis test.
Realm assignment uses realized GBIF occurrence geography and the 11 Holt et al. (2013) terrestrial zoogeographic realms.

The Holt realm map was derived from terrestrial vertebrate assemblage distributions and phylogenetic relationships; it is used here as an external broad-scale zoogeographic partition, not as a butterfly-derived regionalization.
No causal claim about host introduction or range expansion is added.

evaluability_gate.conservative_population: host-taxonomy-adequate species with introduced-host expansion (expected n=191)
